title: Fire Ants Are Heavier Than Water, Yet They Float for Months

scenes.text: Every fire ant is heavier than water. Together, they float.
When a flood hits, the colony links up and builds a raft in just a few minutes.
Their waxy, hairy bodies trap air bubbles, making the raft about seventy-five percent less dense.
Push it under and it pops back up. Poke it and it tightens.
If the ants on top are removed, the ones below climb up and keep the raft the same thickness.
In nature, a raft like this can sail for months. Heavier than water, floating anyway.

description:
Fire ants are denser than water, yet a colony floats by linking its bodies into a raft in minutes.
Trapped air bubbles cut the raft's density by about seventy-five percent, and in nature it can sail for months.
Would you ever step on a fire ant raft?
first_comment: Ants build rafts, bridges and towers. What should they build next?
